metadata.source: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED) & CDS SIMBAD Astronomical Database
metadata.description: Verified astrometric positions, spectroscopic redshifts, morphological classifications, distance estimates, and NASA archival imaging for representative extragalactic targets across all major morphological classes, active galactic nuclei (AGN), and galaxy clusters.

records.name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
records.distanceMethod: Cepheid Leavitt Law & Tip of the Red Giant Branch (TRGB)
records.description: The largest galaxy in the Local Group, heading toward a gravitational merger with our Milky Way in ~4.5 billion years.
records.scientificSignificance: Primary extragalactic laboratory for stellar population synthesis, Cepheid distance calibration, and dark matter halo dynamics.

image.title: Andromeda Galaxy Across Wavelengths
image.caption: Multi-spectral composite revealing Andromeda's spiral arms traced by hot young stars and cool interstellar dust.

images.title: Andromeda Galaxy Across Wavelengths (GALEX/Spitzer/WISE)
images.caption: Multi-spectral composite revealing Andromeda's spiral arms traced by hot young stars (blue, UV) and cool interstellar dust (orange, infrared).

images.title: Andromeda Far-Infrared Dust Ring & Relativistic Core
images.caption: Herschel Space Observatory far-infrared scan exposing the 75,000-light-year ring of cold dust where new stars condense at temperatures barely above absolute zero.

records.name: Triangulum Galaxy (M33)
records.description: The third-largest member of the Local Group, rich in giant ionized hydrogen star-forming regions such as NGC 604.
records.scientificSignificance: Serves as an archetype of unbarred late-type spirals with pure exponential disks and minimal central bulge.

image.title: WISE Infrared Portrait of the Triangulum Galaxy
image.caption: Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) mosaic highlighting cool dust distribution along loose spiral arms.

images.title: WISE Infrared Portrait of the Triangulum Galaxy
images.caption: Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) mosaic highlighting cool dust distribution along loose spiral arms and starburst regions.

images.title: GALEX Ultraviolet View of Star-Forming Complexes in M33
images.caption: Ultraviolet telescope image mapping energetic radiation from hot O and B class stars populating the loose spiral arms of the Pinwheel of the South.

records.name: Whirlpool Galaxy (M51a)
records.distanceMethod: Type II-P Supernova Standard Candle & TRGB
records.description: A classic grand-design spiral galaxy tidally interacting with its companion dwarf galaxy NGC 5195.
records.scientificSignificance: The premier laboratory for density wave theory, spiral shock fronts, and tidal interaction-induced starbursts.

image.title: Spitzer and Hubble Composite of M51
image.caption: Infrared and optical synthesis exposing dust filaments heated by starburst clusters throughout the spiral structure.

observationalMetadata.telescope: Spitzer Space Telescope & Hubble Space Telescope

images.title: Spitzer and Hubble Composite of M51 (Whirlpool Galaxy)
images.caption: Infrared and optical synthesis exposing dust filaments heated by starburst clusters throughout the majestic grand-design spiral arms.

images.title: Chandra X-Ray and Hubble High-Energy Core of M51
images.caption: High-energy X-ray emissions (purple) revealing millions of degrees hot gas envelopes, binary star systems, and active supermassive black hole accretion.

records.name: Sombrero Galaxy (M104)
records.description: Characterized by an exceptionally luminous white central bulge and a prominent dark absorption lane of interstellar dust.
records.scientificSignificance: Hosts one of the most massive central black holes (~1 billion solar masses) in nearby spiral galaxies and an anomalously large globular cluster system.

image.title: Spitzer Space Telescope Sombrero Galaxy Glowing Ring
image.caption: Thermal infrared image piercing the opaque optical dust lane to illuminate a glowing ring of warm circumstellar dust.

images.title: Spitzer Space Telescope Sombrero Galaxy Glowing Ring
images.caption: Thermal infrared image piercing the opaque optical dust lane to illuminate a glowing ring of warm circumstellar dust and star formation.

images.title: Hubble Space Telescope Sombrero Natural Color Portrait
images.caption: Natural-color view revealing the brilliant white bulbous core, rich cluster system of nearly 2,000 globular clusters, and sharp dark silhouette of dust.

records.name: Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC)
records.description: A major satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, housing the Tarantula Nebula (30 Doradus), the most active starburst nursery in the Local Group.
records.scientificSignificance: The fundamental first rung and anchor of the extragalactic cosmic distance ladder.

image.title: Spitzer Infrared View of the Large Magellanic Cloud (SAGE)
image.caption: SAGE Legacy survey reveals millions of newly identified red giants and protostars across the LMC bar and outskirts.

images.title: Spitzer Infrared View of the Large Magellanic Cloud (SAGE)
images.caption: SAGE Legacy survey reveals millions of newly identified red giants and protostars across the LMC bar and outskirts.

records.name: Pinwheel Galaxy (M101)
records.description: A face-on spiral galaxy twice the diameter of our Milky Way containing massive young star clusters and prominent spiral arms.
records.scientificSignificance: Critical target for studying abundance gradients across spiral disks and host to SN 2011fe (Type Ia) and SN 2023ixf (Type II).

image.title: Pinwheel Galaxy in Infrared, Optical, and X-ray
image.caption: Multi-wavelength observatory portrait showcasing hot gas bubbles from supernovae alongside cooler star-forming dust arms.

images.title: Pinwheel Galaxy in Infrared, Optical, and X-ray
images.caption: Multi-wavelength observatory portrait showcasing hot gas bubbles from supernovae alongside cooler star-forming dust arms.
images.instrument: Hubble ACS, Spitzer IRAC, Chandra ACIS

images.title: Hubble Largest High-Resolution Spiral Galaxy Mosaic (M101)
images.caption: Massive 51-exposure mosaic composed of ACS and WFPC2 images spanning 170,000 light-years of spiral structure with billions of resolvable stars.

records.name: Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC)
records.description: A close satellite dwarf galaxy of the Milky Way undergoing severe tidal disruption from gravitational interaction with the LMC.
records.scientificSignificance: Where Henrietta Swan Leavitt discovered the period-luminosity relation in Cepheids in 1908, enabling cosmic distance measurements.

image.title: Spitzer Space Telescope Survey of the SMC
image.caption: Spitzer S3MC survey capturing cold dust filaments and stellar nurseries in a metal-poor galactic environment.

images.title: Spitzer Space Telescope Survey of the SMC
images.caption: Spitzer S3MC survey capturing cold dust filaments and stellar nurseries in a metal-poor galactic environment.

records.name: Sculptor Galaxy (NGC 253)
records.distanceMethod: Tip of the Red Giant Branch (TRGB) & Cepheids
records.description: A dusty edge-on spiral galaxy in the Sculptor Group experiencing furious starburst activity and superwinds in its nuclear core.
records.scientificSignificance: Benchmark nearby target for high-energy cosmic ray acceleration, galactic superwinds, and interstellar dust outflow mechanics.

image.title: GALEX Ultraviolet View of the Sculptor Galaxy
image.caption: Ultraviolet mosaic capturing intense radiation from massive young stars along the disk and nuclear starburst.

images.title: GALEX Ultraviolet View of the Sculptor Galaxy
images.caption: Ultraviolet mosaic capturing intense radiation from massive young stars along the disk and nuclear starburst.

records.name: Barred Spiral Prototype NGC 1300
records.description: Widely recognized as the textbook definition of a barred spiral galaxy, with a central bar stretching over 50,000 light-years.
records.scientificSignificance: Exhibits a 'nucleus within a nucleus'—a secondary nuclear ring structure rotating in the core with its own miniature spiral arms.

image.title: Hubble Space Telescope View of Barred Spiral NGC 1300
image.caption: Sharp ACS detail showing luminous blue young star clusters and dark dust lanes sweeping from the bar ends into graceful spiral arms.

images.title: Hubble Space Telescope View of Barred Spiral NGC 1300
images.caption: Sharp ACS detail showing luminous blue young star clusters and dark dust lanes sweeping from the bar ends into graceful spiral arms.

records.name: Southern Pinwheel (Messier 83)
records.distanceMethod: Tip of the Red Giant Branch (TRGB) & Cepheids
records.description: A nearby grand-design barred spiral dubbed the 'Supernova Factory' due to six recorded historical supernovae within a century.
records.scientificSignificance: GALEX discovery of an enormous extended ultraviolet (XUV) disk four times the size of the optical galaxy.

image.title: GALEX Ultraviolet Portrait of the Southern Pinwheel
image.caption: Ultraviolet exposure revealing young, massive stars forming far out in the galaxy's previously undetected outer gas disk.

images.title: GALEX Ultraviolet Portrait of the Southern Pinwheel
images.caption: Ultraviolet exposure revealing young, massive stars forming far out in the galaxy's previously undetected outer gas disk.

records.name: Messier 87 (Virgo A)
records.distanceMethod: Surface Brightness Fluctuations (SBF) & Globular Cluster Luminosity
records.description: The giant dominant elliptical galaxy at the center of the Virgo Cluster, host to a 6.5-billion-solar-mass supermassive black hole.
records.scientificSignificance: Home to the first directly imaged black hole shadow (Event Horizon Telescope) and a 5,000-light-year relativistic plasma jet.

image.title: Hubble Space Telescope View of M87 Relativistic Jet
image.caption: Synchrotron emission from electrons accelerated to near-light speed along the collimated magnetic jet emerging from M87's central black hole.

images.title: Hubble Space Telescope View of M87 Relativistic Jet
images.caption: Synchrotron emission from electrons accelerated to near-light speed along the collimated magnetic jet emerging from M87's central black hole.

records.name: Messier 49 (NGC 4472)
records.description: The first member of the Virgo Cluster discovered by Charles Messier in 1771 and the brightest galaxy in the entire cluster.
records.scientificSignificance: Hosts over 6,000 globular clusters (compared to ~150 in the Milky Way) and extensive hot X-ray gas halos.

image.title: Hubble Space Telescope View of Giant Elliptical M49
image.caption: Deep ACS optical image highlighting the dense, smooth stellar population typical of aged elliptical systems.

images.title: Hubble Space Telescope View of Giant Elliptical M49
images.caption: Deep ACS optical image highlighting the dense, smooth stellar population typical of aged elliptical systems.

records.name: Messier 89 (NGC 4552)
records.description: A textbook example of an E0 spherical galaxy with an almost circular projected profile on the sky.
records.scientificSignificance: Deep exposures revealed complex nested shells and a 150,000-light-year gaseous plume indicating past merger events.

image.title: Chandra and Hubble Observation of Spherical Elliptical M89
image.caption: Chandra X-ray Observatory detects a high-velocity ram-pressure stripped gas tail behind M89.

images.title: Chandra and Hubble Observation of Spherical Elliptical M89
images.caption: Chandra X-ray Observatory detects a high-velocity ram-pressure stripped gas tail behind M89.

records.name: Centaurus A (NGC 5128)
records.description: The closest active radio galaxy to Earth, featuring a prominent warped dust belt bisecting a luminous elliptical galaxy.
records.scientificSignificance: Direct evidence of a past major merger between a giant elliptical and a smaller spiral, powering colossal radio lobe lobes across 8 degrees of the sky.

image.title: Chandra and Spitzer View of Centaurus A Relativistic Jet
image.caption: High-energy X-ray jet and infrared dust emission tracing matter falling onto the central supermassive black hole.

images.title: Chandra and Spitzer View of Centaurus A Relativistic Jet
images.caption: High-energy X-ray jet and infrared dust emission tracing matter falling onto the central supermassive black hole.

records.name: Antennae Galaxies (NGC 4038/4039)
records.morphologicalType: SA(s)m pec / SA(s)m pec (Colliding Interacting Pair)
records.distanceMethod: Tip of the Red Giant Branch (TRGB) in Tidal Tail
records.description: Two spiral galaxies undergoing a violent high-speed collision, hurling long tidal streams of stars and gas resembling insect antennae.
records.scientificSignificance: The youngest and nearest prototype of major galaxy collisions; exhibits over 1,000 young super star clusters created in shock fronts.

image.title: Hubble Space Telescope Portrait of the Colliding Antennae
image.caption: Stunning cosmic collision creating millions of young stars and brilliant blue starburst clusters.

images.title: Hubble Space Telescope Portrait of the Colliding Antennae
images.caption: Stunning cosmic collision creating millions of young stars and brilliant blue starburst clusters.

records.name: Cigar Galaxy (Messier 82)
records.distanceMethod: Tip of the Red Giant Branch (TRGB) & Cepheids
records.description: An edge-on starburst galaxy with enormous bipolar plumes of glowing hydrogen gas driven out of the disk by collective supernova winds.
records.scientificSignificance: Forms stars at a rate 10 times faster than the Milky Way due to recent tidal encounters with M81.

image.title: Spitzer Space Telescope Infrared Portrait of M82
image.caption: Infrared emission from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) dust molecules lofted 20,000 light-years into the halo by superwinds.

images.title: Spitzer Space Telescope Infrared Portrait of M82
images.caption: Infrared emission from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) dust molecules lofted 20,000 light-years into the halo by superwinds.

records.name: Cartwheel Galaxy (ESO 350-40)
records.description: A spectacular bullseye ring galaxy produced when a smaller companion galaxy plunged directly through its center like a stone in water.
records.scientificSignificance: The expanding density shock wave created a sparkling ring of intense star formation expanding outward at over 200,000 km/h.

image.title: JWST NIRCam and MIRI Portrait of the Cartwheel Galaxy
image.caption: James Webb Space Telescope multi-instrument infrared view piercing through thick dust to expose star formation spokes and active core.

images.title: JWST NIRCam and MIRI Portrait of the Cartwheel Galaxy
images.caption: James Webb Space Telescope multi-instrument infrared view piercing through thick dust to expose star formation spokes and active core.

records.name: Messier 77 (NGC 1068)
records.description: A bright barred spiral containing an energetic active galactic nucleus (AGN) completely shrouded by a dense dusty torus.
records.scientificSignificance: The fundamental prototype for the Unified Model of Active Galactic Nuclei; spectropolarimetry confirmed the presence of hidden broad emission lines.

image.title: Hubble Space Telescope View of Seyfert Core M77
image.caption: Energetic nucleus illuminating ionization cones and a circumnuclear starburst ring.

images.title: Hubble Space Telescope View of Seyfert Core M77
images.caption: Energetic nucleus illuminating ionization cones and a circumnuclear starburst ring.

records.name: Quasar 3C 273
records.angularSize: Point source core with 20″ relativistic jet
records.description: The first quasar ever identified (Maarten Schmidt, 1963) and one of the most luminous active galactic nuclei in the observable universe.
records.scientificSignificance: Luminosity exceeds 4 trillion suns, fueled by a central black hole of 880 million solar masses consuming 100 Earth masses per second.

image.title: Chandra and Hubble View of Quasar 3C 273
image.caption: X-ray and optical composite tracing the 200,000-light-year plasma jet blasting outward from the quasar core.

images.title: Chandra and Hubble View of Quasar 3C 273
images.caption: X-ray and optical composite tracing the 200,000-light-year plasma jet blasting outward from the quasar core.

records.name: Markarian 231 (UGC 08058)
records.description: The nearest Ultraluminous Infrared Galaxy (ULIRG) to Earth, radiating 99% of its colossal energy in the infrared due to dust obscuration.
records.scientificSignificance: Proposed to host a close binary supermassive black hole system producing powerful molecular outflows clearing cold gas from the host galaxy.

image.title: Hubble Space Telescope UV Spectrum View of Mrk 231
image.caption: Ultraviolet analysis revealing evidence for a binary black hole system in the heart of this ultraluminous infrared galaxy.

images.title: Hubble Space Telescope UV Spectrum View of Mrk 231
images.caption: Ultraviolet analysis revealing evidence for a binary black hole system in the heart of this ultraluminous infrared galaxy.

records.name: Virgo Cluster Core (M87 Subgroup)
records.distanceMethod: Mean SBF and TRGB of ~2,000 member galaxies
records.description: The massive heart of the Virgo Supercluster containing over 2,000 cataloged galaxies bound in a common gravitational potential.
records.scientificSignificance: Its colossal gravitational pull creates the 'Virgo-centric infall' where the Local Group and Milky Way are pulled toward the cluster at ~250 km/s.

image.title: Spitzer Space Telescope Infrared Mosaic of the Virgo Cluster Core
image.caption: Wide-field infrared mosaic revealing dozens of member galaxies interacting with the dense intra-cluster gas medium.

images.title: Spitzer Space Telescope Infrared Mosaic of the Virgo Cluster Core
images.caption: Wide-field infrared mosaic revealing dozens of member galaxies interacting with the dense intra-cluster gas medium.

records.name: Coma Cluster (Abell 1656)
records.description: One of the densest known galactic concentrations containing over 1,000 identified galaxies dominated by giant ellipticals NGC 4874 and NGC 4889.
records.scientificSignificance: Where Fritz Zwicky discovered dark matter in 1933 by applying the virial theorem to member orbital velocities.

image.title: Spitzer and Hubble Deep Field of the Coma Cluster
image.caption: Infrared and optical deep exposure showing thousands of ancient yellowish elliptical galaxies bound in the cluster core.

images.title: Spitzer and Hubble Deep Field of the Coma Cluster
images.caption: Infrared and optical deep exposure showing thousands of ancient yellowish elliptical galaxies bound in the cluster core.

records.name: Stephan's Quintet (HCG 92)
records.description: A celebrated compact group of five galaxies, four of which are locked in an intricate gravitational dance generating massive shockwaves.
records.scientificSignificance: Features an enormous shock wave larger than the Milky Way produced as galaxy NGC 7318b plunges through the intra-group medium at millions of km/h.

image.title: JWST NIRCam and MIRI Portrait of Stephan's Quintet
image.caption: James Webb Space Telescope multi-wavelength infrared composite resolving sweeping tails of gas, stars, and shock fronts.

images.title: JWST NIRCam and MIRI Portrait of Stephan's Quintet
images.caption: James Webb Space Telescope multi-wavelength infrared composite resolving sweeping tails of gas, stars, and shock fronts.

records.name: SMACS J0723.3-7327 (JWST First Deep Field)
records.description: A massive galaxy cluster whose immense gravitational field acts as a natural cosmic lens, bending and magnifying the light of galaxies behind it.
records.scientificSignificance: The historic first operational deep-field image from JWST, revealing galaxies as they existed over 13.1 billion years ago.

image.title: JWST First Deep Field SMACS 0723
image.caption: Deepest and sharpest infrared image of the distant universe to date, showing gravitational lensing arcs around SMACS J0723.

images.title: JWST First Deep Field SMACS 0723
images.caption: Deepest and sharpest infrared image of the distant universe to date, showing gravitational lensing arcs around SMACS J0723.
